summary: Round 1 independent review of the three-mode (A=baseline, B=minimal, C=full) GPU events BD1 instrumentation experiment at 45eb20a4. Everything checked matches the agreed scope. Mode A swaps in an empty callback but keeps the same GpuTask(['jungfrau.raw']) declaration, so declared input preparation and the dense gather still happen. A also iterates every event, does the same deviceSynchronize, the same barriers, cache conditioning and NIC/CXI capture. It creates no ReaderAccounting or DeliveryAccounting and records null event_count/callback_events/timestamps/bytes; check_baseline_rows enforces those nulls and returns events/sha/bytes=None. A's only evidence of doing the work is shared: the CXI rx_bytes >= 90% of selected bytes check, cold-cache measured_bytes, provenance and placement. The docs say this plainly and do not claim A proves the event population. Schema isolation holds: load_contract allows baseline only under the abc-v1 schema with phase=overhead, the legacy two-mode schema stays limited to minimal/full, PR phases reject any instrumentation override, perlmutter_adapter.assemble still rejects every overhead schema, and screen()/retry_parent reject ABC captures. The schedule is the exact approved 12-order sequence (pilot: ABC, BCA), and _collect_samples recomputes it and checks it against plan.json. abc_summary uses campaign.paired within each round (right/left-1): B/A=minimal/baseline, C/A=full/baseline, C/B=full/minimal. It always sets overhead_qualified=False, and screen_passed needs a non-pilot run with all three loop intervals equivalent at +/-5%. The pilot-to-main gate is valid: main requires a hash-pinned sealed ABC-schema pilot with pilot=True and the same sources and inputs. The batch script aborts under set -e before main if the preflight fails. Capture seal, index, re-check and reorder rejection reuse the existing collector, and legacy two-mode paths are unchanged (samples without a design key keep the old schema). Timing boundaries match the docs: loop runs from perf_counter start through the GPU sync and the post-loop barrier, taking the max over ranks; process_seconds runs from srun Popen to exit and excludes scheduler confirmation and warmup. Three low, non-blocking findings follow. The hardware preflight and main have not run, so this pass covers code and design readiness only, not any measured result.

findings.evidence: README status says 'implementation and offline validation in progress; no job submitted' while validation-01.json records status pass for the complete offline suite.
findings.requested_change: When recording submission, update the status line to say offline validation is complete (with the reviewed SHA) and give the job ID and its pending/running state.

findings.evidence: Prior GPU BD1 10k retry job 61586044 ran 12 samples in 01:11:32, with measured steps of 3:37-8:06 that grew later in the run. Scaled to 36 main samples plus prefix/site setup and a 6-sample 1k preflight, the job should take about 3.6-5h, or about 5h+ if the late-run slowdown repeats. That fits the user-approved 6h limit but with modest headroom. The fixed-finish/no-rerun policy means a wall-limit kill leaves an unsealed main capture with failed.json absent or partial.
findings.requested_change: No code change required. Record the expected-duration estimate and the timeout-outcome policy (an incomplete main is reported as a failed attempt, with no automatic resubmission) in the notes before or at submission.

findings.evidence: sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS only proves self-consistency of frozen-01 against its own manifest. The reviewed commit is passed in and recorded, never verified by the job (intentional, per OVERHEAD.md:87-90).
